digest.component_or_area: LLM gate economics and cost analysis
propositions: Mean per-completed-ticket LLM gate cost is 11.85 dollars (plan-review 3.02/run, code-review 1.42/run, completion-verification 2.24/run) since Bedrock switch, with per-ticket median 8.15 and p90 21 dollars.

Cheap-model experiments (rounds 1-6) rejected Haiku for agentic review and Nova Pro for completion verification due to accuracy loss or false-accepts, retaining Sonnet and identifying bounded Nova pilots as viable next levers.

Code-review severity axes are structurally inert because blocking decision routes on criterion only (98.2% have blocking_enabled=False) and the 0.95 threshold requires an unachieved 3-way AND (blast_radius=system AND likelihood=high AND reversibility=hard), not because reviewer output is sparse.

Phased ordinal-to-binary migration plan (Phase 0-3) documented without execution; Phase 1-2 convert plan-review ordinal ladders to deterministic kind-set derivation, Phase 3 addresses code-review separately, requiring operator approval before any migration executes.

Deprecation removal analysis found no removable items on schedule (v1.0.0 floor unmet), only tiny gitattributes migration arm is ready now, and Tier 2 (single-pass review, REBAR_LLM_MODEL) candidates for next pre-1.0 breaking window at v0.12.0.

AWS alarm sweep identified two probe-side false-positive defects in observability.sh (cold-start seeding and over-broad pattern matching) causing fabricated metrics and unnecessary firings, with three true-positive review-interrupt bound-exceeded cases suggesting DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX needs tuning, not alarm thresholds.
